Python: $1,000 x (1+60,992.94) = $60,993,940; $1,000 x (1+460.61) = $461,610; ratio 132.1; implied CAGRs 19.8% and 10.6% over 61 years (matches the letter's rounding)

post.instagram_caption:
Would you rather have put $1,000 into Warren Buffett's company in 1964, or into the whole stock market?

From 1964 to the end of 2025, the S&P 500 with dividends gained 46,061% overall, about 10.5% a year. $1,000 became $461,610. Berkshire Hathaway's per-share market value gained 6,099,294%, about 19.7% a year. $1,000 became about $61 million. That's 132 times more, from a gap of about 9 points a year.

What did you guess before the counter stopped?

Source: Berkshire Hathaway 2025 shareholder letter (performance table). Past results don't guarantee future returns. Not financial advice.
